scoring_justification: Recompute defect-state energy and absorption peak energy from agent-provided spectra (tdos.dat, absorption.dat) and compare to paper-reported values within tolerances.

hidden_assets.purpose: Reference defect state energy (3.0 eV) and optical absorption peak (5.3 eV) extracted from the source paper.
hidden_assets.source_provenance: Paper section 20.4, figures Fig. 20.4D and Fig. 20.4I; explicit statements: 'a feature of TDOS at 3.0 eV' and 'The dominant peak has a value of 5.3 eV'.
hidden_assets.why_not_fabricated: These are the exact paper-reported numbers; the checker compares recomputed peak positions against them.

outputs.description: Total density of states for the oxygen‑vacancy supercell. The checker locates the first prominent peak above the valence band maximum (energy > 0) and compares its energy to a hidden reference.
Optical absorption spectrum for the oxygen‑vacancy supercell. The checker locates the energy of the maximum absorption value and compares it to a hidden reference.

output_contract.notes: Both files are plain text with two whitespace‑separated columns. The checker recomputes the relevant peak positions from the supplied data and compares them to the paper‑reported values using appropriate tolerances.

steps.description: Find the energy of the first prominent peak in TDOS above 0 eV (defect state energy). Compare to paper-reported 3.0 eV within ±0.3 eV tolerance, with linear partial credit beyond.
Find the energy of the maximum absorption intensity. Compare to paper-reported 5.3 eV within ±0.3 eV tolerance, with linear partial credit beyond.
